single_node_ceiling.note: Measured single-node limits (HEA-1812; failure onset bisected + verdict reframed in HEA-1813). Two independent ceilings are reported SEPARATELY: (1) hot-path read throughput, and (2) the Argon2id login budget. Do not conflate them. Numbers are hardware-sensitive — see hardware. Single-node only; multi-node/Raft horizontal scale is a separate axis and is not measured here.
single_node_ceiling.hardware: AMD Ryzen 7 7840HS, 16 vCPU, 55 GiB RAM (server + Goose load generator co-resident on one host, loopback)
single_node_ceiling.corpus: resident_corpus=300000 seeded users (realms=5, sessions+revoked per realm), see metadata.dataset_shape

hot_path.note: At 500 concurrent users / 1677 RPS the hot-path journeys (validate, session_lookup, user_lookup, revoke_revalidate) run at p99 = 1-2 ms with ZERO failures, comfortably inside their 1.1-1.5 ms HTTP budgets. Server CPU here is 178% mean / 292% peak of 1600% available (16 vCPU) — the host is far from saturated. The hot path is not the limiter at any sampled concurrency below the load-generator cliff.

argon2id_login_budget.note: The issuance / revoke / revoke_mint journeys perform Argon2id password verification (deliberately expensive, OFF the hot path). At 500u their p99 is 4-7 s under concurrency and they breach the 6 ms HTTP budget BY DESIGN, which is the sole reason overall pass=false even though every request succeeds (0 failures). This is a CPU-cost property of Argon2id, NOT hot-path latency and NOT server saturation. Login throughput is Argon2id-bound; scale it with more cores or an Argon2id work-factor decision, independently of the hot path.

single_node_ceiling.max_comfortable_reason: Last clean steady step: 0 request failures; hot-path journeys p99 = 1 ms within budget; server CPU 178% mean / 292% peak of 1600% available. pass=false is attributable ENTIRELY to the Argon2id login budget (see argon2id_login_budget), not to hot-path or server saturation.

failure_onset.evidence: The 500->600u step flips from 0% to 100% request failures. Across the cliff server CPU COLLAPSES (cpu_mean 178% at 500u -> 5.8% at 600u -> ~0% at 700u+) while RSS stays flat (~3.9 GB, server alive). A saturated server would peg CPU near 1600%; instead it goes idle, which means requests are not reaching it. Failures are client-side 'error sending request for url .../introspect' plus the 60 s client timeout. Cause: the co-resident Goose generator starves for CPU/connections on the shared 16 vCPU host once ~600 closed-loop users contend with the server. This is a TEST-HARNESS ceiling, not a Hearth ceiling.
failure_onset.measured_curve: 500u=1677 RPS / 0% fail (CPU 178%); 600u=100% fail (CPU 5.8%); 700u..2000u=100% fail (CPU ~0%). Collapse is monotone past onset.
failure_onset.to_measure_true_server_cliff: Re-run with the Goose load generator on a SEPARATE host from the server so the two do not contend for the same 16 vCPUs.

single_node_ceiling.reproduction: bash loadtest/scripts/hea1812-curve.sh  (boots 300k corpus once, then sweeps 500 600 700 800 900 1000 1500 2000 u, each with --server-pid for per-step RSS/CPU attribution). Or: make loadtest MODE=steady USERS=500 RUN_TIME=45s HATCH_RATE=500 (clean) then USERS=600 (onset). See README § 'Measured single-node ceiling (HEA-1812/1813)'.

metadata.dataset_shape: realms=5 users/realm=80 sessions/realm=40 revoked/realm=4 (sessions_frac=0.5 revoked_frac=0.1 seed=1) resident_corpus=300000

summary.ceiling_reason: a budgeted journey's p99 breached its HTTP budget — server latency is the limiter; the observed ceiling is the server under test
